scenarios.then: Bear put spread · trade a confirmed breakdown
scenarios.how: A hawkish surprise is a trigger to reassess, not an automatic sell signal.
scenarios.entry: After the release, wait for price to break support and fail to reclaim it. Skip if price holds support or put premiums have already jumped beyond your budget.
scenarios.legs: Buy a put near spot; sell a lower-strike put near your downside target. Use equal size, the same underlying and expiry, typically 7–21 days out.
scenarios.exit: Close both legs near the lower strike, on a reclaim of broken support, or before expiry. A price stop is an exit plan, not a guaranteed fill.
scenarios.risk: Maximum expiry loss: net premium paid. Maximum expiry gain: strike gap minus premium.
scenarios.example: Illustration only: spot 100; buy 100 put / sell 95 put for a net 2. Expiry break-even 98; max loss 2; max gain 3.
scenarios.if: Hot CPI or a hawkish Fed

scenarios.then: Bull call spread · trade a confirmed breakout
scenarios.how: A rate cut can also signal weaker growth. Use the price reaction to confirm the bullish thesis.
scenarios.entry: Wait for price to break resistance and hold a retest. Skip a rejected breakout or a spread whose cost leaves too little upside to your target.
scenarios.legs: Buy a call near spot; sell a higher-strike call near your upside target. Use equal size, the same underlying and expiry, typically 7–21 days out.
scenarios.exit: Close both legs near the upper strike, if price loses the breakout level, or before expiry.
scenarios.risk: Maximum expiry loss: net premium paid. Maximum expiry gain: strike gap minus premium.
scenarios.example: Illustration only: spot 100; buy 100 call / sell 105 call for a net 2. Expiry break-even 102; max loss 2; max gain 3.
scenarios.if: Soft data or a dovish Fed — and price confirms

scenarios.then: Iron condor · sell a range with capped risk
scenarios.how: Consider only while option premiums remain rich versus your expected movement. Selling after volatility has already collapsed misses that repricing.
scenarios.entry: After the release, mark the range and confirm it is holding. Skip an active breakout, thin quotes, or a credit too small for the risk.
scenarios.legs: Sell a put below the range and a call above it; buy a lower put and a higher call as protection. Use equal size, one underlying and one expiry, typically 7–14 days out.
scenarios.exit: Example rule: close all four legs when half the opening credit is captured, when the range breaks, or before expiry. This rule is illustrative, not backtested.
scenarios.risk: Maximum expiry gain: credit received. Maximum expiry loss: wider wing gap minus credit.
scenarios.example: Illustration only: buy 90 put / sell 95 put / sell 105 call / buy 110 call for a net 1 credit. Expiry break-evens 94 and 106; max loss 4; max gain 1.
scenarios.if: Event passes; price stays inside its range

scenarios.then: Long straddle · buy movement only if fairly priced
scenarios.how: A shock alone is not a reason to buy volatility. The remaining move must justify the price of both options.
scenarios.entry: Compare the combined premium with your expected remaining move. Skip if panic premiums already price in that move; staying flat is a valid decision.
scenarios.legs: Buy a call and a put at the same strike near spot, with equal size, the same underlying and expiry, typically 7–14 days out.
scenarios.exit: Close both legs when the expected move arrives, if the catalyst fades, or before expiry. Time decay and falling implied volatility can hurt even after a price move.
scenarios.risk: Maximum expiry loss: total premium paid. Upside gain is uncapped; downside gain is capped by the underlying reaching zero.
scenarios.example: Illustration only: strike 100; pay 3 for the call + 3 for the put. Expiry break-evens 94 and 106; max loss 6. Earlier profit depends on volatility and time remaining.
scenarios.if: More large moves expected; direction unclear

macroNow.title: US inflation came in hot — CPI 3.7%, and producer prices jumped the most since 2022
read: Energy drove it: gasoline +9.1% in CPI, +20.3% at the producer level (BLS).
Higher-for-longer rates are back on the table — rate-cut hopes get pushed out.
The Fed treats this as an energy shock, not a broad price spiral — core CPI is only 2.6%.
If Fed Chair Warsh sounds hawkish (Oct 16, 12:30 KST), BTC is likely to test the $80k put wall; a calm, look-through tone keeps the range.
macroNow.options: Options were already expensive before the print (87th percentile) and puts cost more than calls — the market had paid for protection, so the shock is partly priced.
watch: BTC close vs the $80k put wall

deep.writeup:
Volmex is the premier benchmark index company that created the leading Bitcoin volatility index — **BVIV, known as the “VIX for Bitcoin”** — and is now expanding into compute indices, prediction-market indices and more.

**Where BVIV is used:** Polymarket, Hyperliquid, Bloomberg Terminal, TradingView, Bybit, Raydium, Bitfinex and others.

**Team:** from Staked (acquired by Kraken), IMC Trading, RBC and more.
**Backers:** Anatoly Yakovenko (founder of Solana), Sandeep Nailwal (founder of Polygon), Robot Ventures and more.

**How to use the BVIV perp on Hyperliquid (HIP-3)** — BVIV is 30-day BTC implied volatility:
• Speculate on BTC implied volatility
• Hedge or diversify spot BTC
• Mean-reversion strategies
• Arbitrage against other BVIV Index perpetuals or options

Trade it: https://app.hyperliquid.xyz/trade/mkts:BVIV
Website: https://volmex.finance

projects.name: Gage
projects.what: No-liquidation, fixed-cost loans on Robinhood Chain — the borrower can walk away at expiry, so every loan carries an embedded put
projects.note: V2 live: 7- or 21-day loans against tokenized stocks, memes and Robinhood-ecosystem tokens; lenders and Earn vaults collect the fixed cost

deep.thesis: Options in loan form. Pledging NVDA for USDG with the right to walk away at expiry is economically a put struck at the reclaim cap: the borrower is long the put, lenders are short it and earn the fixed cost as premium. No oracle and no liquidation in the deal path — the decision happens only at expiry.
catalysts: V2 engine live with Earn vaults run by curators
Robinhood Chain stock tokens as collateral
risks: Lenders take the collateral if the borrower walks — a short-put payoff

items.author: Frederik Theissen
items.title: Protection demand rises while options positions expand
items.view: Glassnode reports higher put-versus-call skew and rising options open interest, interpreting the move as increased demand for downside hedges. Its volatility-spread measure also moved closer to zero.

view.title: Post-CPI update
paras: CPI came in hot. Prices rose faster than expected: 3.7% year over year versus the 3.6% forecast, up from 3.4% last month.
BTC sold off hard on it. Price was at 83,471 right before the release, dropped as low as 81,581 within the hour, and closed that move at 81,631. It kept falling after, sitting at 81,131 now.

Here is the weird thing. Normally, once a big number like this is out of the way, options get cheaper because the uncertainty is gone. That did not happen here. Implied volatility actually ticked up a little and is still near the highest levels of the last 90 days. The market is not relaxing.
PPI and Retail Sales print later today, and Fed Chair Warsh speaks Friday, so this week still has more in it.
view.key: Implied volatility rose after CPI instead of falling — the market is not relaxing.
